title: Private Upgrade Runbook Compiler and Stateful Orchestrator
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver a reusable Runbook Compiler and a stateful Orchestrator service for Redwood Private upgrades that enables teams to define, validate, and execute multi-stage migrations with automatic checkpoints, cohorting, and safe rollforward/rollback.

Background: Existing Private upgrades are handled by combinatorial scripts and ad-hoc playbooks. We need a deterministic, machine-readable runbook format plus an execution engine that enforces gates (canary cohorts, healthchecks, compatibility gates) and provides observability hooks and dry-run modes for customers performing VPC or on-prem upgrades.

Scope (MVP):
- Define a compact Runbook schema (YAML/JSON) to express ordered steps, parallel cohorts, pre/post-check probes, transactional migration primitives (quiesce, snapshot, apply, validate), and post-apply sanity checks.
- Implement a Runbook Compiler that validates compatibility matrix constraints (model/runtime version, DB schema version, agent version) and expands high-level steps into executable job graphs.
- Build a stateful Orchestrator service (statemachine-backed) that executes compiled runbooks with checkpointing, idempotent step execution, and per-cohort concurrency controls.
- Integrate rollout gates: automated health probes, SLO smoke tests, approval hooks (manual or automated), and automatic rollback triggers.
- Support dry-run mode (simulate transforms, no writes) and non-destructive preflight checks with clear report artifacts.
- Expose telemetry to Console: per-step timing, success/failure, rollback metrics, and drift detection dashboards.

Out of scope (future):
- Full DB schema migration engine (we will call existing migration runners).
- UI for authoring runbooks (Console integration planned next quarter).

Acceptance Criteria: 
- Runbook schema doc + example library of 6 canonical runbooks (canary upgrade, full cluster upgrade, agent-only patch, LTS pin upgrade, emergency security patch, rollback drill).
- Compiler unit tests with >=90% coverage and model compatibility validation tests.
- Orchestrator runs a synthetic canary upgrade in staging that performs 3 sequential checkpoints and can auto-rollback on a failed health probe.
- Dry-run produces deterministic change-set reports for all runbooks.
- Console telemetry shows an executed staging runbook with correct step-level metrics.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Use an explicit state machine persisted in PostgreSQL to keep the Orchestrator deterministic and easy to recover after process restarts versus relying on ephemeral in-memory coordination. This favors reliability at cost of slightly more storage/ops complexity.
- Keep Runbook language intentionally small and composable rather than a full Turing-complete DSL to reduce user error surface. Transform scripts are allowed as external small executables called with strict timeouts and sandboxes.
- Rollout gating semantics will support both automatic (SLO-based) and manual approvals. We will provide safe defaults tuned for typical Private customers but allow enterprise overrides.

Security and compliance notes:
- All runbook executions must be audited with immutable logs and optionally shipped to customer KMS-backed archive when running in Private.
- Executor processes run in a restricted sandbox; secrets are injected via ephemeral tokens with short TTLs.
- Security review required before GA and for any step that manipulates customer data.
